Here's my 2 cents on what maybe the downside with #HDFCBank merger:   1. HDFC was earlier not under various RBI regulations like SLR, CRR etc. Now that it is merged with HDFC Bank, the combined funds of both entities will have these restrictions. Thus, while their combined size has gone up on paper, in actuality, the funds they have discretion over has reduced.  2. As a general principle, after demergers when managed separately, the businesses are 20% more efficient. I don't have stats to back this up, but it's kind of a conventional management principle. Thus a merger on the flip side will definitely face some inefficiencies ranging  from team cultural conflicts to less focus on niches.  Ofcourse, these maybe overcome by the managements and the stock may do well in coming times given the benefits as well!

#HDFCBank collapsed 4%  HDFC Bank was the top Nifty loser, COLLAPSING 4% intraday! Why? Well, its latest financial assessment of the HDFC-HDFC Bank merger has largely spoiled the mood. Brokerage firm Nomura has also downgraded the stock from a buy to neutral. Here’s what you need to know: 🚨  1) Networth hit:  Due to some accounting tweaks, the combined entity’s book value will be LOWER than HDFC Bank’s standalone book value. FYI – as a result, Nomura has cut HDFC Bank’s FY 2024-2026 EPS estimate by 5% to 9% and book value per share estimates by 7% over the same period. 📉  2) Margin pressure: Excess liquidity + accounting changes could place pressure on the lender’s net interest margins over the next 2-3 quarters. HDFC’s Q2FY24 opening book NIMs were at 2% vs 2.7% in Q1. ⛔  3) NPA build-up: There appears to be a bad loan uptick in HDFC’s corporate book. HDFC’s individual gross NPA ratio stood at 1% for the June quarter vs 0.75% in March. Non-individual gross NPA ratio saw a spike from 2.9% in March to 6.7% in June. Yikes! 📊  A few brokerage firms have cut their target price on the stock. This includes Nomura (Rs 1,970 p/sh → Rs 1,800 p/sh), Citi (Rs 2,200 p/sh → Rs 2,110 p/sh), and Jefferies (Rs 2,100 p/sh → Rs 2,030 p/sh).   That said, most are still bullish, with all price targets representing a 10%-25% potential upside from current levels.
